feature: Security Intelligence Overview (/security-overview) Top Security Risks widget now renders a non-functional 'QUICK FIX' chip (data-testid='finding-quick-fix-chip') next to findings whose title/checkLabel text matches a known write-action domain keyword (users/sign-in, MFA, licensing, groups, teams, SharePoint/OneDrive). Prep for Launch Control write-action integration (#1068-1075/#1077, part of epic #1045) — purely visual, no click handler, not a real per-finding link to a write_action_catalog row (schema investigation in the issue's own comment found no clean join key exists today).
notes: The chip is a client-side, presentational-only text heuristic (TopSecurityRisks.tsx's hasLikelyWriteAction()) — NOT driven by server data, no guaranteed match against any specific tenant's real finding content. This manifest only asserts the structural/always-true parts, not a guaranteed chip.

KNOWN, PRE-EXISTING GAP (confirmed live, not introduced by this change): /api/portal/mission-control/overview (the feed the whole security-overview page's findings/hero live-data hook reads — see useSecurityOverviewLive.ts) is gated `requireRole('CustomerUser')`. The only standard test account (TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL/PASSWORD) is the pre-provisioned testbed 'Assessment' role, which is explicitly BELOW CustomerUser (requireAuth.ts line ~76-83) — so it gets a real 403 on this endpoint. Confirmed by actually running this manifest AND re-running the pre-existing security-overview/hero-pillar-score.json manifest live: both fail at the same page-level 403/empty-render for this account (2/10 steps failed on hero-pillar-score.json, same root cause). This is a test-infrastructure gap affecting the whole /security-overview page's live-data assertions, not specific to this feature. D1/D2/D3 below are marked non-critical so this manifest documents intended coverage honestly without falsely reporting the regression suite red for a pre-existing account-tier gap. Fix: provision a CustomerUser-tier (or above) test account and add its credentials as a new env var, then flip these back to critical.
